review_method: Independent visual inspection of retained original regional maps, legends and basin table and every complete selected baseline path; independent decoding compares exact selected IDs, fragment order, every position and all metadata with immutable baseline inputs. Public validation checks included summaries and factual linkage only.
counted_unit: Distinct logical inventory target IDs, not individual named rivers or verified reach names.

inherited_scope_continuity.supported_name_scope: The complete eastern basin corresponds at regional scale to water beneath the Lake part of the Sandfly Lake label. Its broad northern cap, western notch, eastern indentation and lower eastward arm taper into the southern tip. The full outline was compared with mapped water and surrounding shore. This supports generalized Sandfly Lake association for the selected feature, not equivalence with the entire named lake or extension of that name to connecting river water.

The entire north-south outline corresponds geographically to mapped water between Struga, Ohrid and Pogradec. Its broad northern cap, northeast shoulder, long east and west sides and rounded southern end were compared. Lake Ohrid is a low-confidence geographic naming candidate from literal wording within a partial conservation overlay, qualified by re-designate. Strong shape correspondence does not establish name coverage or naming authority for the complete selected water polygon. No supported whole-water identity or protected-site/water-boundary equivalence is assigned.

naming_scope_details.unassigned_region: Name coverage over the complete selected waterbody, including every source and baseline ring position.
naming_scope_details.follow_up_scope: Resolve independent lake-name authority and name coverage over the complete selected waterbody before promoting the Lake Ohrid candidate. Conservation-area wording is insufficient; no geometry repair is prescribed by this hold.

inherited_scope_continuity.supported_name_scope: The complete northern basin, indented western shore, elongated southwestern lobe, eastern side and southeastern projection correspond geographically to the large water east of Galicica. Prespa Lake is a low-confidence geographic naming candidate from the literal wording in Prespa Lake Monument of Nature over part of the cross-border water. Conservation-area wording does not establish name coverage or naming authority for the entire selected polygon. Great Prespa, exact named-water extent and protected-site/water-boundary equivalence remain unverified; no supported whole-water identity is assigned.

findings.follow_up_scope: No follow-up is required to complete the bounded representative-system assessment. Any separately authorized name application would require headwater/feeder naming evidence, exact river/storage transitions and coastal scope before any per-reach or group scalar name application.
findings.supported_name_scope: The complete selected path descends southeast from its northwestern headwater, curves northeast through the middle corridor, then turns southeast into a broad southern bend and northeast toward the coast. Direct blue Macleay river-line labels support Macleay River as a representative system identity. The long northwestern feeder course is not individually named by the inspected maps, and the modeled mainstem role does not make every part Macleay. Exact feeder-to-main-river name transitions, any river/storage interfaces and the coastal ending remain unassigned at reach level.
limits: Direct blue Macleay river-line wording supports the association; the black Macleay River catchment leader supplies the contextual full form and is not sole identity evidence.
The northwestern upper feeder is not independently named; no guessed tributary name or exact rendered-part partition is assigned.
The original publication is a coarse regional assessment, not a formal naming-register decision or surveyed contemporary mouth map.
Original HydroRIVERS source-coordinate equality and exact source reach-to-rendered-part name mapping are not verified.

confidence.basis: One government regional publication supplies direct mapped Macleay and Manning river-line labels and coarse complete-path correspondence. Hastings has catchment and basin-table context only; exact reach names and formal registry authority remain unverified.

findings.follow_up_scope: Obtain direct river-name or named-station evidence that resolves identity and naming coverage for the complete selected group before promoting the Hastings River candidate. Any separately authorized reach-level or scalar product application also requires headwater/feeder, storage-interface and coastal naming evidence. No geometry repair or new acquisition is prescribed by this bounded hold.
findings.supported_name_scope: The complete selected path descends south from its northwestern headwater and then follows an eastward corridor to the Port Macquarie coast. It corresponds geographically to mapped channels within the Hastings River catchment context. Hastings River is a geographic candidate only: Figure 4.22 provides a catchment leader and Table 4.4 a River basin entry, but no direct Hastings river-line label or named Hastings station was established in the inspected maps. This does not support representative river identity or name coverage over the complete selected group. The modeled mainstem role does not name the headwater or feeder course, storage interfaces or coastal ending. The whole-group naming scope remains on hold.
limits: The Hastings River catchment leader and River basin table entry establish geographic context only, not a directly named river line or whole-group identity.
No named Hastings station was found in the inspected maps; numeric discharge symbols and unlabelled flood-site dots are not named-station evidence.
Table 4.4 describes Port Macquarie and Cowarra as off-creek storages. Their supply relationship does not put either storage on the selected path or establish a river/storage name boundary.
The original publication is a coarse regional assessment, not a formal naming-register decision or surveyed contemporary mouth map.
Original HydroRIVERS source-coordinate equality and exact source reach-to-rendered-part name mapping are not verified.

included_evidence_limit: Only public factual summaries, bibliography and included-file integrity are testable here. The omitted original maps, full selected paths, private decoder inputs and past visual judgments cannot be reproduced by public validation. Representative identity is not a uniform name for every reach or a product approval.
